standard_prerequisites.name: The Picard group of the projective line over a field and the restriction of the twist
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, the lemma computing the Picard group of projective space over a unique factorization domain, together with the identification of the exceptional divisor and the twist on the blowup
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the twist of the blowup generates an infinite cyclic subgroup of the Picard group through its restriction to the exceptional divisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Regular local rings are unique factorization domains and the punctured spectrum has trivial Picard group
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, the lemma that a regular local ring is a unique factorization domain, and Divisors, the lemma on the Picard group of the complement of a closed point
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides a trivialization of any invertible sheaf on the complement of the exceptional divisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: Divisors of invertible sheaves and injectivity of the class group map on a normal scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, the definition of the divisor of a meromorphic section of an invertible sheaf, and the lemma that the class group map is injective for normal schemes
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the trivialization on the complement into a divisor supported on the exceptional divisor and identifies the sheaf with a twist.

core_obligations: Produce an infinite cyclic subgroup (proof lines 755-766): the exceptional divisor is a projective line over the residue field, whose Picard group is infinite cyclic, and the twist of the blowup restricts to the negative of the generator, so the twist generates an infinite cyclic subgroup of the Picard group of the blowup.

Identify an arbitrary class (proof lines 766-783): since the base is a regular local ring it is a unique factorization domain, so the complement of the closed point, which is also the complement of the exceptional divisor in the blowup, has trivial Picard group; hence any invertible sheaf on the blowup is trivialized on that complement by a regular meromorphic section whose divisor is a multiple of the exceptional divisor; injectivity of the class group map for the normal scheme gives that the sheaf is a power of the twist, which completes the identification of the Picard group with the infinite cyclic group generated by the twist.
proof_roadmap: Restrict the twist to the exceptional divisor to exhibit an infinite cyclic subgroup.
Trivialize an arbitrary invertible sheaf on the complement of the exceptional divisor using the unique factorization property.
Compute the divisor of that meromorphic section and use injectivity of the class group map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the Picard group of the blowup of the maximal ideal of a regular local ring of dimension two is infinite cyclic, generated by the twist of the blowup (statement lines 755-761). The proof (proof lines 755-783) restricts the twist to the exceptional divisor, trivializes an arbitrary invertible sheaf on the complement of the exceptional divisor, and identifies its divisor. H2: a complete standard argument in two steps.
